To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the board size is determined by firm size and the board composition is determined by growth options and the presence of a dual CEO-chairman structure.
(1) board size is positively associated with firm size, (2) growth option variables are positively related to board composition, and (3) CEO duality is negatively associated with board composition.

the choice of board size and composition is endogenous to the firm and that the choice of the board is related to firm size, growth options and the presence of a dual position of chief executive and chairman.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the factors which explain the choice of board size and composition.
the factors that might affect the size and composition.
the size and composition (the number of nonexecutive directors) of boards of directors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the choice of board size and composition are endogenous.
the board size is determined by a combination of the firm size and growth options and that board composition is influenced by the existence of a CEO/chairman and growth options.
the board size and composition are not exogenous to the firm and the market.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the board is not just a passive agent but an integral part of corporate governance and its size and composition are endogenously determined.
the board of directors of larger firms in Hong Kong and Malaysia are more independent than their counterparts in Singapore.
there are some similarities and some differences between the three countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the board size and composition is not exogenous to the firm and that it is affected by the firm’s growth options and the choice of the CEO who is also the chairman.
the size and composition are endogenously determined by the characteristics of the firm.
the choice of board size and composition is not exogenous and that it is important to consider firm characteristics in explaining the choice of board structure.
